newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Telecom, Fletcher Energy shine on dull NZ bourse.
newsitem.headline: Telecom, Fletcher Energy shine on dull NZ bourse.

text.p: A sharp lift in Fletcher Energy and Telecom helped propel an otherwise lacklustre New Zealand share market to a firmer finish on Thursday.
Fletcher Energy zoomed 22 cents to $4.03 after rumours that a respected Australian analyst had put out a positive report suggesting it was one of his leading picks.
Telecom ended 13 cents up at $7.35 after a crossing in late trade took it up to $7.37.
The other highlight was the eight cent rise of Lion Nathan after its $150.4 million full-year profit result.
Those three stocks were mainly responsible for lifting the top 40 index 8.72 points to 2,310.16 on volume of $68.4 million.
County NatWest broker Sean Vaughan said the day's pattern of buying in selected stocks was likely to continue. "We are starting to see some clear winners and some clear losers."
Among the losers were Carter Holt Harvey, down five to $3.18 after its 30 percent held Chilean associate, Copec, reported a sharply lower nine month result.
Fletcher Paper continued to underperform, falling two cents to $2.55.
It was not helped by comments from Fletcher CEO Hugh Fletcher who said the paper division profits will be inadequate and there is likely to be more pulp and paper downtime.

The Lion result, at the upper end of expectations, got mixed reviews. Brokers said its poor performance in Australia had been well signalled to the market but some brokers still did not enthuse over the result. "I thought it was a fairly ordinary result. The key to it is the performance in Australia, where, even adjusting for the exchange rate, their earnings are actually in a state of decline," said John Cairns, head of research at Cavill White Securities.
